_about: The heaven hub (plan 7.6f), built the way love, righteousness and glory are: the rows are defined by the Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek, a noun row by the words standing in the verse (or, where a loose rule would take verses that do not show the label, by hand), and a verse sits in every row it fits (match: all). One word, in each language, is the sky and heaven alike: Hebrew שָׁמַיִם, Aramaic שְׁמַיִן, Greek οὐρανός. The Berean prints 'sky', 'air', 'heaven' or 'the heavens' as each verse reads, so the senses are kept apart by row, by what the verse says (the sky and its lights, what falls from it, God's throne and dwelling, where Christ is, where the believer's reward is), and no row says that one is the whole. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/heaven.json.

titles.noun: What the text says of heaven

_forms_why: οὐρανόθεν 'from heaven' (Acts 14:17, 26:13) and μεσουράνημα 'midair' (Rev 8:13, 14:6, 19:17) have no part of speech the builder reads; they are the noun's own forms. ἐπουράνιος and οὐράνιος are adjectives ('heavenly realms', 'your heavenly Father').
_words_why: The concept's own words: Hebrew שָׁמַיִם, Aramaic שְׁמַיִן (Ezra 4-7, Daniel 2-7) and Greek οὐρανός, which the Greek Old Testament uses for the Hebrew; and the Greek words built on it: ἐπουράνιος (heavenly realms, heavenly things), οὐράνιος (heavenly), οὐρανόθεν (from heaven) and μεσουράνημα (midair). The Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek are not said to be one word: a row mixes them only where the text sets them side by side (the God of heaven, Ezra and Daniel beside Jonah and Revelation), and every verse names the word it stands on. Different words that the English also calls heaven or sky are in 'others', apart: the Hebrew שַׁחַק ('skies', 'clouds', 12 verses) and the Greek διοπετής ('fallen from heaven', Acts 19:35). The Hebrew רָקִיעַ ('expanse', as in Gen 1:14) is a different word again, glossed 'expanse' and not 'heaven' or 'sky', so it is not among the hub's words or in 'others'; the Gen 1 verses are here because they also hold שָׁמַיִם ('God called the expanse “sky”'). 'Heavenly beings' and 'heavenly hosts' at Ps 29:1 and 148:2 are other Hebrew words and are not here.
_sense_why: A word counts where MACULA's gloss for it in the verse is heaven, sky, air or expanse. The Berean's English at those verses is whatever it chose ('sky', 'heavens', 'air' in 'birds of the air'); the rows say so where it matters.

others._why: Other words the English calls 'heaven' or 'sky' (as love names φιλέω apart). A word counts when a quarter of its verses are glossed so, whatever their number.
others.title: Other words translated “heaven”, “sky”

_check: 16-verse sample against the Berean text (2026-10-25), 11 of 16 shown outright, 2 after the row's label was widened, 3 failed and fixed: Gen 2:1 ('all their vast array' is not 'host of heaven': out of the host row, stays in 'God made the heavens'); Dan 4:35 (a pronoun in a row of verses that name God: moved to the host row, where the verse says 'the army of heaven'); Rev 14:6 (the Berean prints 'flying overhead' for the Greek mid-heaven: moved from the angels row to the sky row with a note). Widened: Hos 2:21 ('respond' added to the row on the heavens declaring and rejoicing), Jer 23:24 ('He fills heaven and earth' added to the throne row). Wrong turns kept: the first rule for birds named πετεινόν and missed nine Greek verses (the lemma's spelling is not what was typed); the angels rule alone took Gen 24:7, Zech 6:5, Rev 8:10, 8:13, 9:1, 10:8, 11:15, 19:17, 1 Pet 1:12, where an angel and heaven are in the verse but not in the same sentence; a looking-up row was first folded into the catch-all (17 verses) and made a row once the catch-all held 79; 'taken up' and 'coming' were two rows and are one (Acts 1:11 says both).
_review: Not yet reviewed. Contested points the page sets side by side and does not settle: whether believers go to heaven at death or await a new heaven and a new earth (the believer's reward and home, beside the new heaven and the new earth, each row saying the page takes no side); whether the present heaven and earth are renewed or replaced (the row of heavens passing away, shaken, rolled up); whether 'heaven' standing alone is another way of saying God (left as the text has it); who the voice from heaven is, and who 'He', 'the One', 'the Lord' is where the verse names no one (separate rows with notes). The divine persons are by hand: a row about the Father, Jesus or the Spirit is filled with verses where the verse itself names him (or is Jesus' own 'I' and 'Me'); verses that say only 'He' are a row of their own.

rows.note: One Hebrew word, שָׁמַיִם, and one Greek word, οὐρανός, are the sky and heaven alike; the Berean prints “sky”, “heavens” or “heaven” as each verse reads, and the rows below follow what each verse says. Here the host of heaven is bowed to and served as idols (Deut 4:19; 2 Kgs 17:16; 21:3; Jer 8:2; Zeph 1:5; Acts 7:42), stands beside the LORD on His throne (1 Kgs 22:19), worships Him (Neh 9:6), will be punished (Isa 24:21) and cannot be counted (Jer 33:22); Dan 4:35 has “the army of heaven”. The Queen of Heaven is the one to whom incense is burned and drink offerings poured out (Jer 7:18; 44:17-25). In the Berean the title occurs only in Jer 7:18 and Jer 44:17-25, and the page does not say who the figure is. The page sets them down as written.
rows._why: rule: a sun, moon, star or 'host' word in the verse. 'Lights' (Gen 1:14-17) are the expanse's own, in 'God made the heavens'. The Queen of Heaven (Jer 7:18, 44:17-19, 44:25) is added by hand: the Hebrew is 'queen of the heavens' and its words are not the rule's.

rows.label: In the sky and from the sky: birds, clouds, rain, dew, hail, snow, lightning, fire, manna
rows.note: Where the Greek is μεσουράνημα, “mid-heaven”, the Berean prints “midair” (Rev 8:13; 19:17) and “overhead” (Rev 14:6): an eagle flying, an angel flying, birds flying. Where the Hebrew and Greek say “birds of the heavens” the Berean prints “birds of the air”.
rows._why: rule for the birds, clouds and weather words in the verse; fire and bread from heaven added by hand because the rule has no word for them (Gen 19:24, 2 Kgs 1, 1 Chr 21:26, 2 Chr 7:1, Job 1:16, Luke 9:54, 17:29, Rev 13:13, 20:9; Exod 16:4, Neh 9:15, Ps 78:24, 105:40, John 6:31). The Berean prints 'birds of the air' where the Hebrew and Greek say 'birds of the heavens'. The first build's rule missed the Greek 'birds' (Matt 6:26, 8:20, 13:32, Mark 4:32, Luke 8:5, 9:58, 13:19, Acts 10:12, 11:6), eleven Hebrew verses on rain, wind, frost and clouds (Deut 11:11, 28:24, Ps 68:8, 78:26, Jer 14:22, Job 37:3, 38:29, 38:37) and birds (Deut 4:17, Ps 8:8, Prov 23:5, 30:19, Jer 8:7, Lam 4:19, Dan 4:12, 4:21): they were in the catch-all and are added by hand. Rev 14:6 (sample check): the angel flying 'overhead' is the Greek mid-heaven and does not show 'heaven' in the Berean, so it moved here from the angels row; Rev 8:13 and 19:17 ('midair') are added with it.

rows.label: God made the heavens: the expanse called “sky”, the lights set in it, the heavens stretched out
rows.note: One Hebrew word, שָׁמַיִם, is the sky and heaven alike (Gen 1:8: “God called the expanse “sky””), and one Greek word, οὐρανός, is “heaven” in “Our Father in heaven” (Matt 6:9) and the birds' “air”; the Berean prints “sky”, “heavens”, “air” or “heaven” as each verse reads, and the rows follow what each verse says. Ps 148:4 sets “the highest heavens” beside “the waters above the skies”; “the heavens, even the highest heavens” also stand in Deut 10:14 and 1 Kgs 8:27 (the row on God's throne and dwelling).
rows._why: by hand: the verses that say the heavens were made, stretched out, founded or established, and the days of Gen 1 on the expanse. Jer 10:11 is Aramaic ('the gods who have not made the heavens'), the one Aramaic verse in the row.

rows.label: The heavens shaken, darkened, rolled up, or passing away; wonders and signs in the heavens
rows.note: The text says the heavens “pass away” (Matt 5:18; 24:35), are “rolled up” (Isa 34:4; Rev 6:14), “will disappear” and “be destroyed by fire” (2 Pet 3:10, 3:12), and that earth and heaven “fled” (Rev 20:11); the row “A new heaven and a new earth” below sets the new beside them. Most of the Old Testament verses here stand in oracles and poems: against Babylon (Isa 13), against the nations and Edom (Isa 34), over Pharaoh (Ezek 32), in the day of the LORD (Joel 2) and in psalms and Job; the page does not say they speak of the end of the world. Where readers part on whether the present heaven and earth are renewed or replaced, the page takes no side. The wonders and signs are those the text names “in heaven” or “in the heavens” (Joel 2:30; Rev 12:1, 12:3); a sign asked of Jesus “from heaven” (Matt 16:1) is in the row on the opened heavens.
rows._why: by hand, one list of what happens to the heavens and what appears in them. A sign 'from heaven' that Pharisees demand (Matt 16:1, Mark 8:11, Luke 11:16) is a sign sought of Jesus, kept as written.

Dan 4 as the text has it.

rows.label: The heavens opened, parted or shut; a voice, a sound, a light or a sign from heaven
rows.note: Where the verse says only “a voice” from heaven (Matt 3:17; Mark 1:11; Luke 3:22; John 12:28; Acts 11:9; Rev 10:4), the page does not say whose. A sign “from heaven” is what the Pharisees and Sadducees ask of Jesus (Matt 16:1; Mark 8:11; Luke 11:16); the page sets the asking down as written.
rows._why: by hand: opened, parted, rent and shut together (the flood's 'floodgates of the heavens', the opened heaven at Jesus' baptism, 'windows of heaven' in Mal 3:10, the sky shut in Luke 4:25), and a voice, sound or light 'from heaven'. Rev 11:19 and 15:5 ('the temple ... was opened in heaven') are in the throne and temple row, where the verse is about the temple.

rows.label: The heavens declare, praise, rejoice and respond; heaven and earth are called to hear and to witness; voices in heaven
rows._why: by hand: heaven as the one who speaks, praises, rejoices or is addressed, and the loud voices in heaven in Revelation. Ps 150:1 ('His mighty heavens') and Ps 148:2 ('heavenly hosts') are other Hebrew words and stand outside.

rows.label: Looking up to heaven; lifting eyes or hands toward it; stretching a hand toward it; crying to it; reaching, ascending or being caught up to it
rows.note: Going up is asked, wished and refused as well as done: a tower “that reaches to the heavens” (Gen 11:4), a ladder “with its top reaching up to heaven” (Gen 28:12), “Who has ascended to heaven and come down?” (Prov 30:4), “Who will ascend into heaven?” (Rom 10:6) and “David did not ascend into heaven” (Acts 2:34), and “I will ascend to the heavens” (Isa 14:13); Ps 139:8 and Amos 9:2 are in the same row. 2 Cor 12:2 speaks of “a man in Christ” who “was caught up to the third heaven”; the page lists the verse as written and does not number the heavens.
rows._why: by hand: what the verse has someone do toward heaven (look, lift the eyes or hands, stretch out a hand or staff, cry out). It was left in the catch-all in the first build. Exod 9:8, 9:10 (soot) and Job 2:12 (dust) are out: the Berean prints 'into the air' there, so the verse does not show 'toward heaven'; they stay under 'Every other use' with the note.

rows.label: The LORD, God, in heaven; the God of heaven; the Lord of heaven
rows.note: The same phrase, “the God of heaven”, stands in Hebrew (Gen 24:7; Neh 1:4-5; Jonah 1:9), in Aramaic (Ezra 5:11-12; 6:9; 7:12; Dan 2:18-19) and in Greek (Rev 11:13; 16:11); the page lists each as written and does not say the words are one.
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: each verse itself names the LORD, God, the Most High or 'the Lord' who is addressed or speaking as God. Eph 6:9 and Col 4:1 ('a Master in heaven') were in the row of verses that give no name and are now in the row on being taken up (editor's ruling, 2026-10-25).

rows.label: From heaven He looks down, hears, answers, saves and judges
rows._why: by hand: the verses where the one addressed or speaking as God hears, looks, answers or acts 'from heaven'. Ps 85:11 ('righteousness looks down from heaven') names righteousness, not the LORD, and is under 'Every other use'.

rows.label: Heaven is God's throne and dwelling; the heavens belong to Him and cannot contain Him; He fills heaven and earth; the temple in heaven
rows._why: by hand: throne, dwelling place, house and temple 'in heaven', and what the heavens cannot hold. Heb 8:1 and 9:24 are also in the rows of verses on Christ in heaven and of the verses that give no name.

rows.label: Your Father in heaven; our Father in heaven; My Father in heaven
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: each verse names the Father (Jesus' own 'My Father in heaven' and 'your Father in heaven'). The adjective form has 'heavenly Father' (Matt 5:48, 6:14, 6:26, 6:32, 15:13, 18:35).

rows.label: The kingdom of heaven
rows.note: Matthew's own phrase, kept as written (13:11: “the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven”). The matching sayings in Mark 4:11 and Luke 8:10 say “the kingdom of God”. The page sets the phrase down and does not say the two are one.

rows.label: In heaven and on earth: above and below, between heaven and earth
rows._why: by hand: heaven and earth named together as two realms (not as the thing made, which is 'God made the heavens', nor as passing away). 'On earth as it is in heaven' (Matt 6:10) and 'bound in heaven' (Matt 16:19, 18:18) are the text's own phrases and are not glossed.

rows.label: Angels and heaven: in heaven, called from heaven, coming down from heaven, sent to the ends of heaven

not_verses.Rev.14.6: the Berean prints 'flying overhead' for the Greek 'mid-heaven'; the verse does not show 'heaven' (it is in the row of the sky, with a note)
not_verses.Gen.24.7: 'send His angel before you': the angel goes before Abraham's servant; heaven is only in 'the God of heaven'
not_verses.Zech.6.5: the angel names 'the four spirits of heaven'; no angel is in, from or going to heaven
not_verses.Rev.8.10: the third angel sounds his trumpet; it is a star that falls from heaven
not_verses.Rev.8.13: the angels are the three still to blow; the eagle flies in midair
not_verses.Rev.9.1: the fifth angel sounds his trumpet; it is a star that has fallen from heaven
not_verses.Rev.10.8: the voice from heaven speaks; the angel stands on the sea and the land
not_verses.Rev.11.15: the seventh angel sounds his trumpet; the loud voices are in heaven
not_verses.Rev.19.17: the angel stands in the sun; the birds fly in midair
not_verses.1Pet.1.12: the Holy Spirit is sent from heaven; angels long to look into these things
not_verses.Rev.10.5: the angel lifts his hand to heaven: a gesture, in the row of looking up

rows.label: Jesus: “came down from heaven”, “the bread from heaven”
rows.note: Readers part on whether John 6:51-58 speaks of the Lord's Supper or of believing in Christ; the page takes no side.
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: each verse names the Son of Man, Jesus or Christ, or is Jesus' own 'I' and 'My' (John 6:38, 6:51). John 3:31, 6:33 and 6:50 say 'the One who comes from heaven', 'He who comes down', 'the bread that comes down' and are in the row of verses that give no name; 1 Cor 15:47 ('the second man from heaven') likewise.

rows.label: Taken up into heaven (Elijah; Jesus, who has passed through the heavens, at the right hand of God); the Master in heaven (Eph 6:9; Col 4:1)
rows.note: Mark 16:19 stands in the longer ending (16:9-20) that the earliest manuscripts lack. Eph 6:9 (“their Master and yours is in heaven”) and Col 4:1 (“you also have a Master in heaven”) are shown with the verses that name Christ in the same passage: Eph 6:6 (“as servants of Christ”) and Col 3:24 (“It is the Lord Christ you are serving”).
rows._why: by hand: each verse names Elijah, Jesus, Christ, the Lord Jesus or the Son of Man (2 Kgs 2:1 'the LORD took Elijah up to heaven'). Luke 24:51, Acts 1:2, 1:10, 3:21, Eph 4:10, 1 Pet 3:22, Heb 8:1 and 1 Thess 4:16 say 'He', 'Him', 'who' or 'the Lord Himself' and are in the row of verses that give no name. Eph 6:9 and Col 4:1 ('a Master in heaven') joined this row on the editor's ruling, 2026-10-25: Col 3:24 says 'It is the Lord Christ you are serving' (Κυρίῳ Χριστῷ) and Eph 6:6 'servants of Christ', beside Col 4:1 and Eph 6:9 with the same word κύριος; those two verses have no heaven word, so they are quoted in the note and not made rows of the hub. The row was one in the first build with the verses on the coming (Acts 1:11 says both in one verse) and is two again on the same ruling.

rows.label: Coming with the clouds of heaven or from heaven: “One like the Son of Man” (Dan 7:13), “the Son of Man” (Matt 24:30, 26:64, Mark 14:62), “the Lord Jesus” (2 Thess 1:7), “His Son” (1 Thess 1:10)
rows.note: The same words, “coming with the clouds of heaven”, stand in Dan 7:13 (“One like the Son of Man”) and in Matt 26:64 and Mark 14:62 (“the Son of Man”); the page lists them side by side and does not say how they relate.
rows._why: by hand, split from the 'taken up' row on the editor's ruling, 2026-10-25, so that Dan 7:13 is not heard under a New Testament name: it leads, labelled in its own words (the Aramaic is 'like a son of man'), with no door to the Jesus card. Acts 1:11 (taken up and coming back) stands in both rows; Phil 3:20 (a Savior awaited from heaven) is here and in the reward row. No one-verse row: Matt 24:30 and Mark 14:62 repeat Daniel's phrase.

rows.label: Not named in the verse: “He”, “the One”, “the second man”, “the Lord”, “Faithful and True”
rows.note: These verses say “He”, “Him”, “the One who comes from heaven”, “the second man from heaven”, “the Lord” or “Faithful and True” and give no name. Readers take them differently, of Jesus or Christ from the passage around them (for example Luke 24:36, Acts 1:1, John 6:35), of the Father, or otherwise, and the page does not choose. John 6:33 and 6:50 stand beside the bread from heaven in the row on Jesus' “came down from heaven”; Luke 24:51, Acts 1:2 and 1:10 stand beside Acts 1:11 in the row on being taken up.
rows._why: separate from the rows that name Jesus, by hand (the divine persons): a verse that says only 'He' is left as the text has it, never filled by a rule.

rows.label: The Holy Spirit and heaven: descending from heaven, sent from heaven, given by the Father in heaven
rows.note: Luke 11:13 (“your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit”) names the Spirit in the verse as written. Heb 6:4 (“the heavenly gift ... the Holy Spirit”) is in the adjective form. Acts 2:2 (“a sound like a mighty rushing wind came from heaven”) is in the row on a voice, a sound or a light from heaven; Acts 2:4 (“filled with the Holy Spirit”) has no word for heaven, so it is named here and not shown.
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: each verse names the Spirit, the Spirit of God or the Holy Spirit with heaven.

rows.label: Fallen or cast down from heaven: “day star” (Isa 14:12, of the king of Babylon), stars, “the glory of Israel”; Satan (Luke 10:18); war in heaven with the dragon (Rev 12:7-8)
rows.note: Isa 14:12 stands in a song of contempt “against the king of Babylon” (Isa 14:4); Luke 10:18 is Jesus' “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven”; Rev 12:7-8 is war in heaven (Rev 12:9 names the dragon “the devil and Satan”). Readers part on whether these speak of one fall, and the page takes no side. Lam 2:1 casts “the glory of Israel” from heaven to earth and Dan 8:10, Rev 8:10, 9:1 and 12:4 speak of stars; the page sets each down by what its verse says. Isa 14:13 (“I will ascend to the heavens”) is in the row on looking up and going up to heaven.
rows._why: by hand: the verses that say something falls, is cast down or is driven out of heaven (stars, a king, Satan, the glory of Israel in Lam 2:1) and the war in heaven. Visions: connected, not interpreted.

rows.label: Reward, treasure, a name written, an inheritance, a house and citizenship in heaven
rows.note: What the text says is kept, stored or written “in heaven” (Matt 6:20; 1 Pet 1:4; Luke 10:20), an eternal house in heaven (2 Cor 5:1) and citizenship in heaven with a Savior awaited from there (Phil 3:20). Where Christian traditions part on whether believers go to heaven at death or await a new heaven and a new earth (the next row), the page takes no side; the adjective form has “heavenly realms”, “heavenly calling” and “heavenly Jerusalem”.
rows._why: by hand: what is laid up, written or kept for the believer 'in heaven', and the house and citizenship. The verses are given as written; none says 'at death', and the page does not add it.

rows.label: A new heaven and a new earth; the holy city coming down out of heaven
rows.note: The text has “I will create new heavens and a new earth” (Isa 65:17) and “the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make” (Isa 66:22); it speaks of a new heaven and a new earth where righteousness dwells (2 Pet 3:13) and of the holy city coming down out of heaven from God (Rev 21:2, 21:10). Where Christian traditions part on whether believers go to heaven at death or await this, the page takes no side; the row above has what the text says is kept in heaven, and the row on the heavens passing away has 2 Pet 3:10-12 and Rev 20:11.

rows.label: “Heaven” standing alone: “against heaven”, “from heaven or from men”, “Heaven rules”
rows.note: The text says “heaven” where one might expect a name; the page leaves it as written and does not say whom it stands for. The same chapter has “the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind” (Dan 4:25) just before “Heaven rules” (Dan 4:26); the page sets the two side by side and does not say they name one and the same.
rows._why: by hand: 'heaven' as the one sinned against, appealed to or ruling, with no other word beside it.

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Among them the sky as iron or bronze (Lev 26:19; Deut 28:23), smoke rising to the sky (Josh 8:20), soot and dust thrown “into the air” (Exod 9:8, 9:10; Job 2:12, where the Berean prints “air” for the Hebrew word for heaven), the heavens that endure (Deut 11:21; Ps 89:29; 119:89; Jer 33:25), the heavens not pure in His eyes (Job 15:15), a witness in heaven (Job 16:19), the God who rides the heavens (Deut 33:26; Ps 68:33), His glory covering the heavens (Hab 3:3), silence in heaven (Rev 8:1) and Peter's sheet let down from heaven and taken back up (Acts 10:16; 11:5; 11:10).

rows.label: Your heavenly Father; My heavenly Father; “you have one Father, who is in heaven” (Matt 23:9)
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: each verse names the Father as 'your heavenly Father' or 'My heavenly Father'. Matt 23:9 ('you have one Father, who is in heaven') joined on the editor's ruling, 2026-10-25: it has the Greek οὐράνιος, the word this row is built on, and names the Father in the verse.

rows.label: Heavenly realms, things, bodies, calling, gift, country, Jerusalem, kingdom, host, vision
rows.note: Among them blessings, a seat and rulers “in the heavenly realms” (Eph 1:3; 2:6; 3:10; 6:12), “a heavenly calling” (Phil 3:14; Heb 3:1), “a better country, a heavenly one” and “the heavenly Jerusalem” (Heb 11:16; 12:22) and “His heavenly kingdom” (2 Tim 4:18). Where Christian traditions part on whether believers go to heaven at death or await a new heaven and a new earth, the page takes no side.
